newsitem.title: OMAN: Gulf states vow to fight violence, "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Gulf states vow to fight violence, "terrorism".

text.p: Gulf Arab countries on Monday pledged to fight what they said was an upsurge in "extremism" and "terrorism", supporting any official measures to defend national security.

Interior ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) said at the end of a one-day meeting in the Omani capital that they had reached their conclusions after reviewing recent security developments in the region and across the globe.

"The ministers observed an increase in extremism, violence and terrorism, resulting in terror against innocent people, destruction of buildings...and destabilisation of the countries' security," they said in a final communique.

"The ministers reaffirm their determination to fight such phenomena in all their forms...by intensifying consultation, cooperation and coordination between security forces in the member states," it said.
The GCC -- a political, military and economic alliance -- groups Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait and Qatar.
In Bahrain, at least 27 people have been killed since anti-government protests by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community broke out in December 1994.
One man has been executed for killing a policeman in the protests and three other men have been sentenced to death for deadly arson attacks.

Security concerns in Saudi Arabia have increased after two bombings of U.S. targets killed 24 Americans and two Indians since November 1995. Four Saudis who confessed on state-run television to roles in the November blast were executed in May.
The ministers' statement said the GCC viewed the security of all member states as an indivisible whole.

"Any threat to any member state's security is considered a threat to the security of all member states," it said. "The ministers expressed their support for any measures taken by any member state to secure its stability."
The GCC's Assistant Secretary General Abdelaziz Bu Ali said earlier on Monday the ministers' findings would be submitted to GCC leaders at their summit in Qatar next month.
